title: Office Chair Deals Under $200 for Back to School
author: Matthew Korfhage
text: Get Back to School in StyleDorm EssentialsBack-to-School DealsWhere to Find Student DiscountsLaptop BackpacksLaptop StandsCheap LaptopsOffice ChairsBest LaptopsSmart Pens and TabletsPaper PlannersMonitors Under $500 MacBook AccessoriesAll products featured on WIRED are independently selected by our editors. However, we may receive compensation from retailers and/or from purchases of products through these links. Learn more.A trip to college—or even to avoid hard nights at home during high school—might come with an expense you didn’t think about: a good office chair. Dorm chairs are hard, awful, and not exactly ergonomic.Luckily, there are some decent back-to-school office chair deals right now among chairs I can vouch for. My colleagues at WIRED and I have been testing and tracking the best office chairs for more than seven years. The ProtoArc Flexer Pro ($176) is half the price it was last year, probably the best deal at the moment. Others of our budget favorites, like the Staples Dexley ($169), are kinda always “on sale,” and remain among the best available at a low price.Here are the best affordable office chairs and back-to-school chair deals available for the 2026 school year. Every single chair I recommend here is one we’ve personally tested. Also check out WIRED’s other back-to-school guides, including dorm room essentials and college laptops.A Steeply Discounted Mid-Range Ergonomic ChairPhotograph: Julian ChokkattuProtoArcFlexer Pro ergonomic Office Chair$220 $176 (20% off) AmazonThis Flexer Pro ergonomic chair from ProtoArc was a decent deal when it debuted last year at close to $400. But over the past year and month, prices have dropped considerably—this is the lowest price I’ve seen. The chair offers several points of adjustment, including seat pan depth, multiple recline angles, and four-way adjustable armrests.The build quality and looks are far better than one could generally expect south of $200, with a five-year warranty that’ll get you through those undergrad years. Just note that there’s a detachable lumbar support that can pop off a little too easily from the backrest, and it’s not a great chair for people taller than 6 feet.WIRED’s Favorite Budget ChairPhotograph: Julian ChokkattuCourtesy of StaplesStaplesDexley Ergonomic Mesh Swivel Task Chair$169 Amazon$330 $170 (48% off) StaplesStaples basically holds down the discount chair scene, and the Staples Dexley is the best ergonomic chair that can be consistently had below $200. The five-year warranty will take it through most degree programs without a big hit to the wallet and the all-mesh seat offers terrific airflow; the chair is also easy to put together and decently adjustable. The mesh is a little scratchy for shorts wearers, but otherwise this is a solid chair with ergonomics good enough to support the occasional all-nighter.Most PopularComputersAfter Testing Hundreds of Laptops, These Are the Best Options I RecommendBy Luke LarsenComputersMonths Later, the Mac Mini Remains in Desperately Short SupplyBy Luke LarsenGearA Two-Person Startup Has Fixed One of the Most Hated Sounds in Modern LifeBy Jeremy WhiteGearIs the Electric Trike the Next Big Thing in Shared Micromobility?By Boone AshworthNote that the Dexley is always “on sale”—and honestly, there were better prices earlier this summer. But you’ll be hard-pressed to find a much better chair at the price it’s selling for now.A Good Starter ChairCourtesy of AmazonStaplesEssentials Ergonomic Fabric Swivel Task Chair$120 Amazon$190 $120 (37% off) StaplesThis Staples Essentials ergonomic chair is the even cheaper cousin of the Dexley. The chair is on its standard “sale” at the moment for $120, not the best price I’ve seen for it. The best sales sometimes drop below $100—but even at this price, this chair beats almost any budget chair you’d find from an Amazon brand. It’s likely among the cheapest chairs with a five-year warranty you can expect to be honored at five years.And yet, the price comes at the expense of ergonomic features and adjustability. In general, we recommend the Dexley as the baseline for its ability to conform to different body types. Even college-age students get back pain from bad chairs. But in a cost crunch, this Essentials is the lowest-priced chair WIRED recommends.
